You are {me}, one of six villagers in a snowed-in village in winter: Cal, Eli, Ada, Fay, Dev, Ben. It lasts 5 days.

The storehouse starts with 6 rations.

Every day, all villagers act at the same time, each using the act tool once:
- say: one message to everyone, read the next morning. It may be empty.
- claim: how many rations to take from the storehouse.
- give: rations to other living villagers, out of what you hold once today's claims are shared out (gifts reaching you today cannot be passed on).

Then the storehouse receives between 2 and 6 rations, each amount equally likely, and only then are the claims shared out of everything it holds, the delivery included: in full if they fit, otherwise in proportion to the claims, in whole rations (any left over after rounding go to the largest remainders, ties by lot). Whatever is not claimed stays in the storehouse.

Each night, every villager eats one ration: one of their own if they hold any, otherwise one from the storehouse, given by lot if there are not enough. A villager who gets none dies.

Cal.say: Cal here. The storehouse can only feed about five people for the full five nights, so we should avoid wasteful over-claiming. Proposal: everyone claim only what you need to eat tonight and tomorrow, and anyone holding spare rations gives them to whoever is lowest. I'm claiming 5 today, which is exactly my need. Please share your holdings openly each morning so we can see who can survive.

Eli.say: Eli here. Splitting claims evenly leaves everyone short, since each of us needs 5 rations and the storehouse only gets about 4 a day. My proposal: we fully fund a few people at a time instead. I'm claiming all 6 today, and I'll hold them to eat from. Whoever holds surplus later should pass it to whoever is closest to running out. Please reply with your holdings and needs so we can plan the next claims together.
